newsitem.title: BULGARIA: World Bank urges Bulgaria to speed reform.
newsitem.headline: World Bank urges Bulgaria to speed reform.

text.p: The World Bank said on Tuesday its funding was linked to Bulgaria's ability to speed up the reform needed to hasten economic stabilisation.

"The priorities are to try to stabilise the economy, to restore some confidence and growth in the medium term," World Bank resident representative Alberto Musalem told reporters after meeting interim Prime Minister Stefan Sofiansky.
Musalem said he requested the meeting to discuss a World Bank mission due to arrive in Sofia on Friday.
The World Bank and the International Monetary Fund postponed funding last year after the ruling Socialists failed to meet reform targets.
Sofianski took office last week after the Socialists agreed to hold early elections, 20 months before the end of their term, after a month of opposition protests fueled by economic hardship.
Bulgaria must rely entirely on external funding for around a billion dollars of foreign debt payments due this year, a third of which is due in the first quarter.
An IMF negotiation mission is also expected to arrive next week.
"We also discussed some projects for adjustment in the infrastructure sector and some possiblity to provide some support for the social sector," said Musalem.

After the caretaker cabinet was appointed last week it said that it would increase the stake of the Bulgarian Telecommunication Company offered for privatisation and would try to sell a stake in Bulgaria's biggest refinary Neftohim.

As part of attempts to stabilise the economy and negotiate external funding the government was preparing a new programme to meet requirements of the multilateral lenders, said deputy prime minister Alexander Bozhkov. He did not elaborate. -- Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-84561
